q: How should we explain a big change in BRSR emissions from last year?
title: Explain a big change in BRSR emissions
short: Split the change into its causes: more or less production, a different fuel or power mix, a new emission factor, a change in boundary, or a corrected error. Give the size of each in tonnes and restate last year if the method changed, so readers compare like with like.

ul: Activity: output went up or down.
Mix: a fuel switch, solar added, or more grid power.
Factor: a new CEA database version or a new fuel factor.
Boundary: a plant added, closed or sold.
Correction: last year's figure had an error.
One line per cause with the tonnes it explains.
Show intensity alongside the total, since output changes move totals.
If a factor or boundary changed, restate last year's figure on the new basis and say so.

p: Do not credit reductions to projects when the drop came from lower output or a new factor. A reviewer will check.

senseible: Senseible reads kWh, litres and kg from electricity bills and fuel invoices into a dated record per site, with the factor and source on every line, and prepares BRSR drafts from that data. Reports are self-declared drafts.
